value.rationale: Y-elements are semantic universal fixed-point solutions central to the finite-vs-free BMI problem. Beyond known existence, the finding completely classifies permitted cardinalities in every finite size and realizes every admissible right-regular algebraic shape with a provably minimal two-point overhead. The exclusion of exactly one defective point is a sharp structural phenomenon, not a numerical artifact, and motivates analysis of fixed-point-selector abundance in finite combinatory models.
